gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each candidate costs to run around the clock as an Immich server. By the makers' own drive-access wattage at the August 2026 US average residential rate of 18.16¢/kWh, ChatGPT's top pick, the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus, has the highest rated draw: 42.36 W = 371 kWh = $67.39 a year. The UGREEN DXP2800 comes to 16.38 W = 143 kWh = $26.06 a year, about $41 a year (about $207 over five years) less. Separately, no result maps the Synology DS225+'s 6 GB memory ceiling against Immich's 8 GB recommendation: the DS225+ can never meet it.
standout_why: I compared against the four pages ChatGPT cited: docs.immich.app Requirements, Backup and Restore, the FAQ, and GitHub mobile-backup.md. I also checked our current page. The Requirements page gives only the 6 GB minimum and 8 GB recommended RAM, 2–4 cores and the SSD advice. It names no NAS, no wattage and no electricity cost (opened 2026-11-17). The FAQ has no NAS models, power or RAM-use figures (opened 2026-11-17). ChatGPT's answer gives prices but no running cost, and it never notes that the DS225+'s maximum memory equals Immich's minimum. Our current page says the DS225+ is 'below Immich's 6 GB minimum until upgraded'. It doesn't say that even fully upgraded it stops at 6 GB, below the 8 GB recommendation, and it has no wattage or running cost.
decides: This supports a 2-bay N100 box (UGREEN DXP2800) as the value Immich pick for an iPhone photo library. It ships with Immich's recommended 8 GB, takes up to 16 GB, and is rated at the lowest drive-access draw among the Docker-capable candidates: about $26 a year against $46–67 for the 4-bay boxes ChatGPT recommended. That is about $207 saved over five years against ChatGPT's #1, the DXP4800 Plus. The Synology DS225+ drops out because its 6 GB ceiling never reaches 8 GB. The DS925+ ships with 4 GB and needs a RAM upgrade before it meets the recommendation. Treat cross-brand wattage gaps as rough, because the makers test differently (see notes). The UGREEN-to-UGREEN gap is like-for-like, since UGREEN tested both units the same way.
